title: Resumable stream segmentation and tool-call interop
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Implement a resumable HTTP streaming strategy that unifies chunk framing, idempotent replay, and explicit function/tool-call boundaries for the Core API. Goal: allow clients to reconnect mid-response and resume without duplicating side effects (tool calls) while remaining compatible with older eventstream clients. This work touches the runtime framing layer, protocol negotiation headers, SDK helpers for resume tokens, and console observability to surface replay and gap metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits monotonic chunk IDs and per-chunk integrity hash; clients can request resume from a chunk ID and receive a deterministic tail of the stream.
Tool/function-call events are emitted with a two-phase boundary (CALL-START / CALL-END) so resumed streams do not replay external side effects; server provides call dedup token for idempotency.
Older clients (legacy eventstream with no resume header) continue to function unchanged; protocol negotiation uses an Accept-Resume header and falls back safely.
SDKs (node/python) expose a high-level resume() helper that accepts a last-seen chunk id and transparently handles reconnection and call dedup tokens.
Automated integration tests cover reconnect during: plain text streaming, structured JSON streaming, active tool call, and multiplexed chat sessions.
Metrics and logs appear in console: resume-count, duplicate-chunk-drops, call-dedup-success, average-resume-latency.
Performance regression <= 3% p50 token latency for steady-state streaming with framing enabled compared to baseline.
Security: resume tokens must be short-lived and signed; token validation failures are audited and do not reveal internal state to clients.

decisions: Use 64-bit monotonic chunk ids (unsigned) so clients can safely represent offsets across large responses.
Resume tokens will be JWT-like signed blobs containing tenant, stream-id, last-chunk-id, and expiry. Server validates signature and expiry; tokens rotate via KMS.
Tool/function-call dedup will rely on server-provided call-dedup-token and idempotency table with TTL equal to response window; this avoids forcing all function providers to be idempotent.
Backoff/retry: client should implement exponential backoff with jitter; server provides Retry-After when resource constrained.
Compatibility: negotiate via Accept-Resume: negotiate=on|off; default off for backward compatibility. When both sides support resume, server enables content framing.
We will not attempt to replay external tool side effects server-side; instead we assert and expose call-dedup-tokens so downstream integrations can be idempotent-aware.
Chunk integrity uses SHA-256 prefix (8 bytes) to keep overhead low while catching corruption across proxies.
